teaching.hint: How large can a right-side product become before its exact value can no longer affect any comparison?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Any product above the largest possible left sum cannot match it, so such products may be safely capped.
solution_outline.approach: Compute the total sum, then build suffix products saturated just above that sum. Sweep indices left to right with a running left sum and return the first equality.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: Every unsaturated suffix entry is exact; a saturated entry exceeds every possible left sum. The running sum contains exactly the positions before the current index.
solution_outline.correctness: At each index the two maintained quantities match the definition. Saturation cannot create a false equality, and scanning in order returns the smallest match.
solution_outline.complexity: O(n) time and O(n) auxiliary space, using wide arithmetic and checking before multiplication.
solution_outline.pitfall: Multiplying an unbounded suffix product can overflow and accidentally appear equal to a prefix sum.

common_wrong_turns: Include the current element on either side
source_fidelity_notes: Empty-side identities and strict-before/after boundaries are retained.
